concepts.def: 1940s jazz style — fast, harmonically dense, soloist-led.
Replacing a chord with a related more complex one (e.g. tritone sub).
Replacing V7 with a dominant 7 a tritone away.

walkthroughs.body_html: Bebop crystallised in Harlem clubs (Minton's, Monroe's) from 1942. Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie drove the style — fast tempos, sixteenth-note phrases, chromaticism, complex chord substitutions.
Tritone substitution replaces V7 with a dominant 7 a tritone away — e.g. G7 becomes Db7 — producing chromatic bass and shared tritone (the chord's defining interval).
Parker's Ko-Ko (recorded November 1945), based on the chord changes of Cherokee, exemplifies bebop virtuosity at lightning tempo (around 300 bpm).
